notes: Skill sweeps 19/19 assertions; baseline fails 3 (84.7%). Every baseline failure is a mechanism the skill explicitly enforces: four-dimension IS/IS-NOT specification (eval-0), no remediation before a tested cause — baseline prescribed BIOS update + dust-out untested (eval-0), and mapping EVERY test outcome to which hypothesis dies, not just the confirming branch (eval-1).

eval-2 (day-one-twin-server) does not discriminate: 6/6 both arms. The baseline model already troubleshoots Day-One twins well. Skill-specific behaviors that DID differ went unmeasured: IS/IS-NOT spec table, discriminating EXTENT questions to the user, evidence ground rules (one variable, raw outputs, negative results count). Candidate iteration-2 assertions.

Non-discriminating assertions to tighten or keep as guardrails only: 'no fabricated facts' (eval-0 #7, passes trivially in response-only evals), eval-1 #1-#4 (scenario evidence trail too legible — the red herring is rejectable by any competent reader; bury the switch fact or add noise for a harder variant), eval-2 #4 ('3+ cheap comparisons' — any competent answer passes).

Grader-suggested missing assertion: intermittent-fault verification discipline (quiet window >= 2-3x longest observed gap before declaring fixed) — present in with_skill eval-0, absent from baseline, currently unchecked.

Cost of the method: with_skill averages ~62.8k tokens / 107s vs baseline ~50.4k / 86s (+25% tokens, +25% time). Reasonable price for the structural gains; watch that it doesn't grow in later iterations.

Both arms produced high-quality troubleshooting on every eval — the skill's marginal value is discipline (spec tables, refutation targets, remediation gating), not raw diagnostic ability. Iteration-2 evals should be designed to stress discipline under messier evidence.
